Risks and Watchouts

  • Limited social data (13 posts) – The small sample size makes trend signals weak and may not represent broader consumer sentiment.
    What to do: supplement with larger, more recent datasets or conduct additional social listening to strengthen evidence.
  • Outdated social posts (702–699 days old) – The newest Instagram and Pinterest posts are over 700 days old, reflecting past rather than current interest.
    What to do: acquire fresh social media data or perform a new trend scan to capture up-to-date signals.
  • Stale Amazon snapshot (158 days old) – Product availability, pricing, and popularity may have changed since the snapshot date.
    What to do: refresh Amazon data or integrate a live API to ensure decisions are based on current market conditions.
  • No moderate or stronger social support for segments – All identified trend segments have only weak evidence, raising uncertainty about their viability.
    What to do: validate these segments with additional sources or delay investment until stronger signals emerge.
  • AI-generated product attributes from listing text – Automated labeling can introduce errors or misclassifications.
    What to do: perform a manual audit or cross-check a sample of labels to confirm accuracy before using them in strategy.
  • Illustrative images instead of real product photos – The images provided are not actual product visuals, which may mislead design or aesthetic decisions.
    What to do: source authentic product images for accurate visual analysis and consumer testing.
